hints: Look closely at the acid formula, how many acidic $\text{H}$ atoms can it lose to form its anion?
Removing both $\text{H}^+$ ions from $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$ leaves the ethanedioate ion $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, while aluminium is always $\text{Al}^{3+}$.
Balance a $3+$ cation against a $2-$ anion to get zero overall charge, think of the lowest common multiple of 3 and 2.
walkthrough:
**Find the charge on the ethanedioate ion**

Think of the acid as having two carboxylic acid groups joined together. Each $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ can lose one $\text{H}^+$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+$$

**Recall the charge on aluminium**

Aluminium is in Group 13 and always forms the same simple ion in its salts. It loses three electrons.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{Al} \rightarrow \text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^-$$

**Balance the charges to make a neutral salt**

We need total positive charge = total negative charge. The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$2 \times (+3) + 3 \times (-2) = 0$$
So we need 2 $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions for every 3 $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions, giving $\text{Al}_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3$.

options.A: This suggests one $\text{Al}^{3+}$ balances one $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, giving a net $+1$ charge, not neutral. It ignores that the acid is diprotic and the anion has a 2- charge.
options.B: This would be correct if ethanedioate were $1-$, like ethanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$. But ethanedioic acid loses two protons, so $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ with three of them gives a total $6-$ against only $3+$, leaving a $3-$ charge overall.
options.C: This has the right 2:1 ratio of Al atoms but forgets the brackets and the correct number of anions. One $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ cannot balance two $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions, the charges do not cancel.
options.D: Two $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions give $+6$ and three $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions give $-6$, so the salt is neutral. Brackets are needed because three whole polyatomic ethanedioate units are present: $\text{Al}_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3$.
